intent: Trace the estimated daily oxygen need in India from March 2020 through March 2021 and identify when it reached its highest level.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
Does the video trace the estimated daily oxygen need in India from March 2020 through March 2021 and identify when it reached its highest level?
The estimated daily oxygen need in India reaches its highest level in March 2021 at 10.501155 million m³, which is greater than all other monthly values in the period.

units.claim: All 1 required series appear in panel single chart.
accept: every required series is visible and correctly labeled in this panel
reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: The estimated daily oxygen need in India changes over time from March 2020 through March 2021, starting at 0.200751 million m³ in March 2020, rising to a local peak of 4.501733 million m³ in September 2020, declining to 1.500578 million m³ in February 2021, and then rising sharply to 10.501155 million m³ in March 2021.
units.computation: Trace the line across the ordered x-values from Mar 2020 to Mar 2021, noting the overall shape: initial rise, mid-period decline, and final sharp increase.
accept: Describes an overall upward trend from March 2020 to March 2021 with a mid-period decline.
Mentions the rise to September 2020, decline through February 2021, and sharp rise to March 2021.
Uses the line to show how oxygen need evolves over the stated period.
reject: Claims oxygen need decreased monotonically over the whole period.
Omits the mid-period decline or the final sharp rise.
Describes only isolated points without conveying the trend.

units.claim: The estimated daily oxygen need in India reaches its highest level in March 2021 at 10.501155 million m³, which is greater than all other monthly values in the period.
units.computation: Compare the value at March 2021 (10.501155) against the maximum of all other points; the next highest is September 2020 at 4.501733, so March 2021 is the global maximum.
accept: Identifies March 2021 as the time of the highest estimated daily oxygen need.
States the maximum value is about 10.5 million m³.
Shows that the March 2021 point is the peak of the line.
reject: Identifies September 2020 or any other month as the highest level.
Fails to name the peak month.
Claims the maximum occurs at the start of the period.

optional_valid: Mentions the specific value 4.501733 million m³ for September 2020 as a local peak.
Notes that the lowest value is 0.200751 million m³ in March 2020.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal explanations for the changes in oxygen need.
Comparisons with other countries or regions.
Claims about data after March 2021 or before March 2020.
Exact percentage changes unless computed from the table.
review_notes: The intent asks for a trace over the period and identification of the highest level, yielding two semantic units: one trend and one extremum.
The x-axis label mentions April 2021 but the data ends at March 2021; the claim follows the data table.
